before: An iterator produces items through next. map transforms items lazily: constructing it does not eagerly build a vector. A closure uses |argument| expression syntax; here it doubles each integer when requested.

into_iter on the vector takes ownership of its elements. next needs a mutable iterator binding and returns Option: Some(item) when available, None when exhausted. Each call advances; it does not restart the source.

before.question: If the first next() call is removed, what does the remaining call print?
choices: None because constructing map exhausts it.

after.question: If the first next() call is removed, what does the remaining call print?

after.explanation: The remaining request is the first request, so it doubles 2.
